w:r.w:t: The Rice Field After the Rain
Ang Umahan sa Humay Human sa Ulan
Target Grade Level: Grade 6
Location / Setting: Barangay Quezon, Tagbina, Surigao del Sur
Subject Integration: English & Science (Agriculture / Weather and Plants)
Theme: Careful Decision-Making
Learning Competency: Identifying the Main Idea, Understanding Cause and Effect, and Analyzing Character Actions
The Story / Ang Istorya
Page 1
English:

Early one morning in Barangay Quezon, Tagbina, Surigao del Sur, twelve-year-old Lino walked with his father, Mang Tomas, toward their rice field. Heavy rain had fallen throughout the night, and the field was covered with puddles of water. Their young rice plants were still standing, but some parts of the field looked muddy and weak.
Mang Tomas stopped and carefully observed the field. “We need to check the soil and water level before we do anything,” he said.
Bisaya:

Sayo usa ka buntag sa Barangay Quezon, Tagbina, Surigao del Sur, naglakaw si Lino, dose anyos, uban sa iyang amahan nga si Mang Tomas padulong sa ilang umahan sa humay. Kusog ang ulan tibuok gabii, ug napuno og tubig ang umahan. Nagbarog pa ang ilang gagmay nga tanom sa humay, apan ang ubang bahin sa umahan lapok ug daw huyang.
Mihunong si Mang Tomas ug maampingong gisusi ang umahan. “Kinahanglan nato susihon ang yuta ug kadaghan sa tubig una ta mohimo og bisan unsa,” ingon niya.
Page 2
English:
Lino looked at the field and noticed that one side had too much water. He wanted to open the small water passage immediately so the water could flow out.
“Father, I can open the canal now. The rice plants might be damaged if we wait,” Lino said.
Mang Tomas shook his head. “We should not decide too quickly. Let us first check if the soil is already soft enough and whether the water is still rising or slowly going down.”
Bisaya:
Gitan-aw ni Lino ang umahan ug namatikdan niya nga sobra kadaghan ang tubig sa usa ka bahin. Gusto niya nga ablihan dayon ang gamay nga agianan sa tubig aron mogawas kini.
“Tatay, pwede nako ablihan ang kanal karon. Basin madaot ang mga tanom sa humay kung maghulat pa ta,” ingon ni Lino.
Milingo si Mang Tomas. “Dili ta angay magdali sa pagdesisyon. Susihon una nato kung humok na ba kaayo ang yuta ug kung nagkadaghan pa ba ang tubig o hinay-hinay na kining naug,” iyang tubag.
Page 3
English:
Lino agreed to wait. Together, they walked around the field and checked the water level in different areas. They also looked at the rice plants and the small drainage canal.

After observing carefully, they noticed that the water was already slowly going down. The soil near the canal was also very soft. If they opened the canal too quickly, the rushing water could carry away some of the soil and damage the young rice plants.
Lino realized that his first idea might have caused more harm than good.
Bisaya:
Miuyon si Lino nga maghulat. Magkauban silang milibot sa umahan ug gisusi ang lebel sa tubig sa nagkalain-laing bahin. Gisusi usab nila ang mga tanom sa humay ug ang gamay nga kanal sa tubig.

Human sa maampingong pagsusi, namatikdan nila nga hinay-hinay na diay nga naug ang tubig. Humok usab kaayo ang yuta duol sa kanal. Kung ablihan nila dayon ang kanal, basin maanod ang yuta ug madaot ang mga gagmay nga tanom sa humay.
Nasabtan ni Lino nga ang iyang unang ideya mahimong makahatag hinuon og dugang kadaot.
Page 4
English:
“Now I understand, Tatay,” Lino said. “I wanted to solve the problem quickly, but I did not check what might happen next.”
Mang Tomas smiled. “That is why careful decisions are important. Before making a choice, we should look at the situation, think about the possible results, and choose the safest action.”

They decided to wait until the water dropped more. Then, they slowly cleared the drainage canal using their hands and small tools. They made sure that the water flowed gently instead of rushing through the field.
Bisaya:
“Karon nasabtan na nako, Tatay,” ingon ni Lino. “Gusto nako nga masulbad dayon ang problema, apan wala nako hunahunaa kung unsay mahimong mahitabo sunod.”

Mipahiyom si Mang Tomas. “Mao nga importante ang maampingong pagdesisyon. Sa dili pa mohimo og desisyon, kinahanglan nato tan-awon ang kahimtang, hunahunaon ang posibleng resulta, ug pilion ang pinakaluwas nga buhaton.”

Naghulat sila hangtod nga mas moubos pa ang tubig. Dayon, hinay-hinay nilang gilimpyohan ang kanal gamit ang ilang mga kamot ug gagmay nga gamit. Gisiguro nila nga hinay ang pag-agos sa tubig aron dili madaot ang umahan.
Page 5
English:
By afternoon, the water had drained properly, and the rice plants remained standing. Lino felt relieved because they had protected the young plants without damaging the soil.
As they walked home, Lino said, “I learned that making a quick decision is not always the best decision. Sometimes, we need to stop, observe, and think before we act.”
Mang Tomas nodded proudly. “A careful decision can protect not only the rice field but also the hard work of the whole family.”
Bisaya:
Pag-abot sa hapon, hapsay nang nahubas ang tubig, ug nagbarog gihapon ang mga tanom sa humay. Nalipay ug nakaginhawa si Lino kay naprotektahan nila ang mga tanom nga wala madaot ang yuta.
Samtang nagpauli sila, miingon si Lino, “Nakat-on ko nga ang dali nga desisyon dili kanunay mao ang pinakamaayong desisyon. Usahay, kinahanglan ta mohunong, mosusi, ug maghunahuna una ta molihok.”
Milingo si Mang Tomas ug mipahiyom. “Ang maampingong desisyon makapanalipod dili lamang sa umahan sa humay kondili usab sa kahago sa tibuok pamilya.”
Page 6
English:

The next time heavy rain came, Lino remembered what his father had taught him. Instead of acting immediately, he first observed the field, checked the water level, and thought about the possible effects of his actions.
He learned that careful decision-making means using what you see, asking questions, and thinking about the consequences before choosing what to do.
From then on, Lino became more careful not only in the rice field but also in his daily life.
Bisaya:

Sa sunod nga higayon nga kusog na usab ang ulan, nahinumdom si Lino sa gitudlo sa iyang amahan. Imbis nga molihok dayon, una niyang gisusi ang umahan, gitan-aw ang lebel sa tubig, ug gihunahuna ang posibleng epekto sa iyang buhat.
Nakat-on siya nga ang maampingong pagdesisyon nagpasabot sa paggamit sa imong nakita, pagpangutana, ug paghunahuna sa mahimong resulta sa dili pa mopili kung unsay buhaton.
Sukad niadto, nahimo nang mas maampingon si Lino dili lamang sa umahan sa humay kondili usab sa iyang adlaw-adlaw nga kinabuhi.
COMPREHENSION CHECK-UP
Directions: Read each question carefully. Choose the letter of the correct answer.
1. What is the main lesson of the story?
A. Always work quickly to solve problems.
B. Think carefully before making a decision.
C. Avoid helping other people.
D. Ignore problems until they disappear.
2. Where did the story take place?
A. In a busy city in Manila.
B. In a school in Cebu.
C. In Barangay Quezon, Tagbina, Surigao del Sur.
D. In a market in Davao City.
3. What happened to the rice field after the heavy rain?
A. The rice plants dried up.
B. The rice field became flooded, and the soil became soft and muddy.
C. The soil became hard and dry.
D. The rice plants were ready for harvest.
4. Why did Mang Tomas tell Lino to wait before opening the drainage canal?
A. He wanted Lino to go home.
B. He wanted Lino to observe the water level and soil condition first.
C. He did not want to help Lino.
D. He wanted the rain to continue.
5. What could have happened if they had opened the canal too quickly?
A. The rice plants would grow faster.
B. The water would disappear without any risk.
C. The rushing water could carry away the soil and damage the young rice plants.
D. The soil would become dry immediately.
Answer Key:
B
C
B
B
C
